subject: Science
title: Use less, use again, sort waste
objective_verbatim: Describe how we can care for our environment: reduce, reuse and recycle (sustainability).
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 1.98 on 687 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 7.98 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to choose ways to care for a place.
success_criteria: I can use a thing again.
I can say why I chose it.

retrieval.question: What helps hold your body up?

stages.pupil_text: Look at the kit. Point to one thing you know.
stages.adult_text: Offer one safe, clean sheet and one clean tub; use first–then and a visual cue.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say it, sign it or point.
stages.adult_text: Ask all three retrieval questions orally; source cells and answers are in this note.

stages.pupil_text: Watch me sort one clean card.
stages.adult_text: Pre-teach the four words with the kit; model the full sort; then ask the show-me check.

stages.pupil_text: Sort the clean cards with us.
stages.adult_text: Use the part-done model, then the live card sort; offer F and H routes without changing the goal.

stages.pupil_text: Show one choice at the same time.
stages.adult_text: Use symbol or point by default. Apply the 3-in-4 rule and a parallel hinge if needed; include one quiet-minute reset.

stages.pupil_text: Choose a clean item. Show what you can do.
stages.adult_text: One adult supports pupils and the other holds the group; swap over the week. Hands-on item or card is valid.

stages.pupil_text: Show one step. Hear one next step. Try it.
stages.adult_text: Give VF and a specific NS(+); let the pupil edit (//). Include one quiet-minute reset.

stages.pupil_text: Show how you know. Tell your teacher.
stages.adult_text: Hear the pupil by speech, sign, point, drawing or writing; use the response to choose the next starter. Include one quiet-minute reset.

cfu.question: I write on the back. Do I need a new sheet?

hinge.question: A clean cloth bag is ready for another trip. Which choice uses less new material?

options.diagnosis: Takes a new item rather than reusing one.
Reuses the clean item before needing a new one.
Adds new items without a need.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model with a clean refillable tub and ask the parallel hinge. Do not save or score.

parallel_hinge.question: A clean bottle can be refilled for another drink. What uses less new material?

misconceptions.misconception: Reusing and recycling mean the same thing.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil says the clean tub must be broken down before it can be filled again.
misconceptions.correction: Show the same tub used again; recycling makes a new thing from old material.

misconceptions.misconception: Any old thing goes in any recycling bin.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil puts all example objects in one real bin without checking.
misconceptions.correction: Use labelled practice trays and check local bin instructions before a real bin is used.

we_do.support: Point to the back. Say Use less.
we_do.stretch: Why use the back before the bin?

tiers.F: Pick one way to use less.
tiers.M: Show one item you can use again. Say why.
tiers.H: Which uses less new stuff: fill a clean tub again or take a new tub? Why?

stems.H: I choose ____ because it needs less ____.

tiers.go_deeper: Could one safe item be used again before it is sorted for a bin? Show how.
tiers.early_finisher: Tub or sheet: pick a first step for each. Which avoids a new item? Why?

adaptations.cognition_learning: Give a three-card visual sequence and one action at a time; retain the full goal.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Model point/sign/speech choices, pause for an answer, and use the same three labelled cards.
adaptations.semh: Offer a private first–then cue and a planned pause before the hinge; re-enter with one choice.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Use large clean card or a tray that stays in place; point or use an accessible switch/keyboard rather than grasping.
adaptations.eal: Pair for spoken rehearsal in any language, then use the same visual words and M/H challenge; do not move the pupil to F for language alone.

F.a: Clean tub, or another safe example.

F.q: What side of the sheet can you use?

facts.claim: Using the blank back of a sheet avoids taking a new sheet for this task.
A safe, clean tub can be used again before recycling; reuse means using an item again.
Recycling means reprocessing old materials into new products, materials or substances. Earlier page said “new material” without this distinction.
Material describes what an item is made of; example can is metal.
Use less / reuse comes before recycling in the waste hierarchy, where feasible and safe.
Check local acceptance before putting a clean can in a real collection bin; earlier card implied a collection route from material alone.
A safety check is needed before reusing an item; this practice uses clean classroom kit only.
Use less: one bottle in place of several new bottles is an example of preventing waste.
Use again: a clean, safe tub can hold pencils rather than being thrown away.
Recycle: only put an accepted can in the correct local collection route.
New transfer hinge and parallel: A clean cloth bag is ready for another trip. Which choice uses less new material? Correct: Use the cloth bag again.

stages: Arrival (5 min): Look at the kit. Point to one thing you know. Staff: Offer one safe, clean sheet and one clean tub; use first–then and a visual cue.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say it, sign it or point. Staff: Ask all three retrieval questions orally; source cells and answers are in this note.
I Do (5 min): Watch me sort one clean card. Staff: Pre-teach the four words with the kit; model the full sort; then ask the show-me check.
We Do (7 min): Sort the clean cards with us. Staff: Use the part-done model, then the live card sort; offer F and H routes without changing the goal.
We Do 2 (5 min): Show one choice at the same time. Staff: Use symbol or point by default. Apply the 3-in-4 rule and a parallel hinge if needed; include one quiet-minute reset.
Independent (8 min): Choose a clean item. Show what you can do. Staff: One adult supports pupils and the other holds the group; swap over the week. Hands-on item or card is valid.
Review (4 min): Show one step. Hear one next step. Try it. Staff: Give VF and a specific NS(+); let the pupil edit (//). Include one quiet-minute reset.
Exit (3 min): Show how you know. Tell your teacher. Staff: Hear the pupil by speech, sign, point, drawing or writing; use the response to choose the next starter. Include one quiet-minute reset.
